comment: Measured on 4 Nov 2026 on Linux: start about 2 s and 30.6 MB, first round +2.9 MB, second round +0.0 MB. Raise a limit only on purpose, in the same pull request as the change that needs it, saying why. 11 Nov 2026: the start limit went from 36 to 37 MB. Giving the small text sizes names (Styles/Sizes.axaml), so a style can change them, costs about 0.7 MB at start (35.8 to 36.5 MB): each of the sidebar's and Overview's small texts now follows its name instead of holding a typed number. Pages opened later cost no more than before. 12 Nov 2026: the start limit went from 37 to 38 MB. A new install now shows the day, the timer, chat and a clock beside the dock, which costs about 0.9 MB at start (36.4 to 37.3 MB) after the dock's menus and group lists were made to build only when asked for; with nothing beside the dock it costs nothing. 17 Nov 2026: the start limit went from 38 to 39 MB. Notifications are kept under a bell in the sidebar (both its wide and folded forms, about 0.2 MB) and every Needs you line can be dismissed, so the line's one button for taking it off now shows on every line, not only on mail (about 0.3 MB): 37.8 to 38.4 MB. To keep it to that, Today's Done and Dismiss add no parts to a row (the list takes the click on the row's own label; a button per row cost 20 MB with 199 things on a day) and the bell's list is built when first opened. 25 Nov 2026: the start limit came DOWN from 39 to 21 MB. The made-up day has 199 things on it and Overview drew every one; Today now shows the first 12 with Show more under them, which took the start from 38.8 to about 17 MB and the first frame from 2.2 to 1.5 s. Finding it showed what a row costs: about 120 KB each, because every Border, TextBlock and Button carries a style record for each class style in Styles/Controls.axaml that names its type (61 for Border, 25 for TextBlock, 54 for Button), whether or not it has the class. So a list that can be long is capped or virtualised, and a class style used by one page belongs in that page, not in Controls.axaml. The first-round figure rose from 2.7 to 3.6 MB, as one-off costs the long list used to pay at start are now paid by the first page opened. The same day made three pages heavy while open, which the measure now reports for every page and holds to openPageMegabytes: Planner's Home 98 MB, Diary 91 MB and Calendar 73 MB, each drawing a row for all 199 things. Their lists now show the first 12 too (Home sends you to My tasks for the rest; Diary's to-dos and Calendar's picked day have Show more), which brought them to 20, 33 and 34 MB. The heaviest page open is now about 34 MB (Calendar, Diary, Settings), so the limit is 45.
